name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Add a "safe patch" rule to auto-apply only formatting tweaks (spaces, line breaks, indentation) to our own codebase. The trade-off is we skip deeper logic fixes, but we keep the repo clean with zero human effort. This keeps the improvement loop fast and safe while we decide how to handle bigger changes.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "skipping deeper logic fixes"—it’s that formatting-only patches create a false sense of cleanliness while masking rotting logic. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* formatting tweaks to *third-party* code (where we don’t own the logic) and gatekeep our own codebase with human review. Settle it by running a controlled experiment: measure how often formatting-only patches hide real bugs in our own code vs. how often they prevent noise in third-party code.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is that auto-applying formatting-only patches to our own codebase trains us to tolerate superficial cleanliness while ignoring the decay beneath—like polishing a rusted engine. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* formatting tweaks to *generated code* (where human logic isn’t at stake) and enforce manual review for our own logic-heavy changes. Settle this by running a pilot on generated code first, then measuring whether the false sense of cleanliness actually improves or masks real rot.
